query: If P is true and Q is false, what is P implies Q?
reasoning:
1. Recall the rule: "P implies Q" is false in exactly one case — when P is true and Q is false; it is true in all other cases.
2. Given: P is true and Q is false. Check if this matches the one false case from step 1 (P true, Q false). It matches.
3. Since the inputs match the only false case, the result is false.
